questions.learningObjective: apply the doctrine of judicial review to a concrete legal fact pattern
questions.stem: Consider this: A court reviewing a statute asks whether a statute exceeds constitutional authority. The statute has a severability clause. Which statement best states the governing legal rule on these facts?

options.text: A court may amend an unconstitutional statute so that it becomes constitutional on these facts.
A duly enacted statute can never be reviewed because the legislature is supreme on these facts.
Judicial review means hearing an appeal from a legislature's vote on these facts.
Judicial review lets a court measure a statute against the constitution and refuse to enforce a provision that conflicts with it on these facts.

questions.explanation: Review is a power to judge compatibility, not to legislate. When a conflict is found, the court declines to give the offending provision effect and leaves replacement to the political branches. Here the decisive point is the power to declare legislation unconstitutional, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether the court may invalidate or may only suggest. Keep the inquiry on the power to declare legislation unconstitutional.

questions.stem: Consider this: A litigant challenging an enactment reviews an agency's factual finding. The statute has a severability clause. Which statement best states the governing legal rule on these facts?

options.text: Severability allows the court to keep enforcing the invalid provision under the circumstances described.
If a statute contains a severability clause or its parts can function independently, a court may strike the offending part while leaving the rest in force under the circumstances described.
One unconstitutional section always invalidates the entire statute under the circumstances described.
A court may never leave part of a statute standing because that would rewrite it under the circumstances described.

questions.explanation: The remedy should match the defect. Where the valid portions can operate on their own and the legislature indicated they should, a court preserves them rather than discarding more than necessary. Here the decisive point is severability and partial invalidation, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether the surviving provisions can work alone. Keep the inquiry on severability and partial invalidation.
